subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: For WebChat/Codex sends, should `chat.send` be allowed to return `started` before the Codex native thread has proven it can accept or rotate the turn?
rationale: The source can still ACK before dispatch and durable user-turn persistence, while the right repair could be fail-fast, force-rotate, persist-before-ACK, health-surface recovery, or a combination; automation should not choose that contract silently.

options.title: Require liveness before `started`
options.body: Make `started` mean the send has passed dispatch/turn-start liveness or has safely rotated to a fresh native thread, returning a visible failure otherwise.

options.title: Keep async ACK but add recovery
options.body: Preserve current fast ACK semantics and add durable pending-turn recovery plus user-visible blocked-state diagnostics when Codex cannot start.

options.title: Close as mitigated by adjacent fixes
options.body: Treat #88207 and the July terminal-liveness work as sufficient only if maintainers accept no current-main replay of the reported 212k-thread wedge.

recommendation.title: Require liveness before `started`
recommendation.body: Make `started` mean the send has passed dispatch/turn-start liveness or has safely rotated to a fresh native thread, returning a visible failure otherwise.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged overflow-rotation work is the closest current-main implementation surface for choosing the native-thread liveness contract.
